course_name_en: Accompanying Studies Science, Technology and Society
prerequisites: Enrollment is required for all examinations of the modules in the accompanying studies. Participation in the accompanying studies is regulated by § 3 of the statutes. Registration for the accompanying studies for KIT students is done by selecting this module in the student portal and self-booking a performance. Registration for courses, performance reviews, and exams is regulated by § 8 of the statutes and is generally possible shortly before the start of the semester.

learning_outcomes.text: Graduates of the accompanying studies in Science, Technology and Society possess a solid foundational knowledge of the relationship between science, public, economy, and politics, and acquire practical skills that prepare them for dealing with media, political consulting, or research management.

Participants gain insights into disciplinary social and humanities discussions on the subject of science, technology, and society and learn to think interdisciplinarily to initiate innovations, shape societal processes, and engage in dialogue with politics and society.

Participants acquire epistemological, economic, social, cultural, and psychological perspectives on scientific knowledge and its processing in science, economy, politics, and the public, in addition to their subject-specific knowledge.

They can assess and weigh the consequences of their actions at the interface between science and society as students, researchers, and future decision-makers, as well as individuals and part of society, based on their disciplinary professional training and the interdisciplinary teaching in the accompanying studies.

Participants can categorize the chosen in-depth contents of the accompanying studies within the foundational context and independently and exemplarily analyze, evaluate, and scientifically express themselves about the contents of the chosen courses in written and oral form.
Graduates can analyze societal topics and problem areas and critically reflect on them from a socially responsible and sustainable perspective.

syllabus_topics: Basic Unit (4 ECTS): Ring lecture "Science in Society" and a basic seminar.
Specialization Unit (12 ECTS): Courses on humanities and social science subject areas: "On Knowledge and Science", "Science in Society", and "Science in Societal Debates".

Subject Area 1: On Knowledge and Science (internal perspective of science, origin of knowledge, distinguishing scientific and non-scientific statements, assumptions, goals, and methods of knowledge generation, handling researchers' biases, analyzing structures of scientific explanatory and prognostic models, mechanisms of scientific quality assurance).

Subject Area 2: Science in Society (interactions between science and different societal areas, scientific knowledge in societal decision-making processes, societal demands in scientific research, specific functional logics of different societal areas, goal and action conflicts in transfer processes between science and economy, politics, journalism, scientific discovery to innovation, scientific policy consulting, influence of economy and politics on science, criteria for journalists using scientific findings, origins of anti-science sentiment, strengthening societal trust in science).

Subject Area 3: Science in Societal Debates (current debates on major societal issues: sustainability, digitalization/artificial intelligence, gender equality/social justice/educational opportunities, handling of arguments, own biases, contradictory information in factual debates, deeper and more nuanced conduct of factual debates than often seen publicly).
Supplementary achievements (up to 12 ECTS from the accompanying study offerings).
assessment_rules: The overall grade of the accompanying studies is calculated as a credit point-weighted average of the grades of the examination performances achieved in the specialization unit. After successful completion, participants receive a graded transcript and a certificate issued by FORUM. Supplementary achievements do not contribute to the overall grade but can be listed on the transcript upon request.
